Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

disgrace noun

also shame, disgraceful, shameful, dishonourable, scandalous, be a disgrace to, dishonour, dishonor, that’s a disgrace

classical

Traupman 151
Traupman 304

dēdecus, dēdecoris n.

noun, third declension

disgrace, dishonour, shame

Other words

  • ignōminia, ignōminiae f. — disgrace, public dishonour

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Traupman 151, 157; Traupman 304

    Properly the loss of one’s good name (nōmen), a mark of public disgrace.

  • dēdecorī esse (+ dative) — to be a disgrace to

    predicative dative with esse and the dative of the person · also used · classical · Cic. Off. 1.139: ampla domus dēdecorī saepe dominō fit (Lewis & Short s.v. sōlitūdō; s.v. dēdecus without saepe); Ter. Haut. 2.3.93: dēdecorī est (Lewis & Short); Traupman 151; Traupman 304

  • ignōminiōsus, ignōminiōsa, ignōminiōsum — disgraceful, shameful

    also used · classical · Quint. 7.1.8 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 151, 157

  • dēdecōrus, dēdecōra, dēdecōrum — disgraceful, dishonourable

    also used · classical · Plaut. Bacch. 5.2.73 (Lewis & Short); Traupman 151

    Lewis & Short: very rare.

  • flāgitiōsus, flāgitiōsa, flāgitiōsum — scandalous, shameful

    also used · classical · Traupman 157

Examples

  • Edepol facinus improbum est!

    That’s a darn disgrace!Traupman 305
